signals.title: CHF/NOK — G10 Bilateral Theme + Geopolitical Shock
signals.text: CHF outperforms across the G10 board with a 1W average of +0.829% across 6 pairs, while NOK trails as the laggard at -0.659% across 2 pairs, generating a wide 1.488% G10 spread. Headline news of an Iranian IRGC mine strike on a tanker in the Strait of Hormuz establishes a acute geopolitical risk bid that favors CHF safe-haven flows over energy-linked currencies. SNB Chairman Schlegel confirmed the Swiss economy continues to grow while noting the central bank stands ready to intervene if price stability is at risk. CHF ESI of +35.9 reinforces this underlying fundamental strength against NOK's +15.5 print. The SNB 0.00% vs Norges Bank 4.50% rate gap leaves CHF at a 450bp carry disadvantage, yet geopolitical risk flows dominate carry mechanics. Trade bias: Short NOK/CHF, safe-haven premium overrides carry disadvantage. Catalyst: Norges Bank interest rate decision today at 09:00 UTC. Risk: De-escalation headlines in the Middle East cause rapid unwind of safe-haven CHF bids back into high-carry NOK.

signals.title: USD/JPY — Carry Support vs Escalation & Options Skew
signals.text: USD/JPY trades at 158.18, holding above its SMA20 at 157.95 and SMA50 at 157.37 while remaining capped below the 200-day moving average at 158.61. A 275bp OIS carry advantage (SOFR 3.97% vs TONA 1.23%) continues to anchor the core long USD stance, but geopolitical headlines regarding the Strait of Hormuz tanker strike create downside shock risk. The 25d risk reversal sits at -1.93, indicating strong put skew as institutional market participants actively buy downside protection against a rapid carry unwind. CFTC leveraged funds hold a net short JPY position of -19,224 contracts (94th percentile, z +1.57), leaving positioning stretched and vulnerable to forced covering. With VIX at 16.6 (normal volatility), carry remains intact for now, though 160.00 remains the key structural level that has previously triggered intervention warnings. Trade bias: Long USD/JPY, carry-supported above moving-average cluster. Catalyst: US Initial Jobless Claims today at 13:30 UTC. Risk: VIX spikes above 25 or JPY safe-haven flows accelerate, triggering a sharp unwind of leveraged JPY shorts.

signals.title: GBP/USD — CB Decision + Extended COT Positioning
signals.text: GBP/USD trades at 1.3475, standing firmly above its SMA20 (1.3331), SMA50 (1.3369), and SMA200 (1.3425) technical cluster. The OIS spread of +23bp (SOFR 3.97% vs SONIA 3.74%) mildly favors USD carry, while the nominal policy rate spread between the Fed (4.00%) and BoE (3.75%) shows a 25bp advantage for the dollar. CFTC data shows leveraged funds hold +20,016 net long contracts in GBP, down by -9,646 contracts WoW as spec longs trim exposure ahead of central bank event risk. Option markets reflect light hedging with a 25d RR of -0.39 alongside 1M IV at 5.3% vs HV30 at 4.3% (+1.0% VRP). Trade bias: Neutral GBP/USD, technical momentum limited by central bank event risk. Catalyst: BoE Interest Rate Decision and Monetary Policy Report today at 12:00 UTC. Risk: Dovish voting split on the MPC triggers swift downside test of the 1.3425 SMA200 level.

signals.text: USD/SEK trades at 9.733, positioning below its SMA20 (9.905) and SMA50 (9.834) while holding above the SMA200 at 9.478. signals.title: EUR/USD — Stalled Trend + Options Volatility Neutrality
signals.text: EUR/USD trades at 1.1247, maintaining a spot location above its 20-day SMA at 1.1198 but capped beneath the 50-day (1.1364) and 200-day (1.1552) moving averages. Fed 4.00% vs ECB 2.65% establishes a 135bp policy rate spread and a +153bp OIS carry advantage in favor of USD, capping extended upside structure. CFTC data reflects heavy EUR speculative short positioning with leveraged funds net short -99,557 contracts (2nd percentile, z -1.78), indicating deep positioning crowding. 1M ATM implied volatility sits at 5.6% against 30-day realized volatility of 4.3%, displaying a modest 1.3% vol risk premium, while the 25d risk reversal at -0.10 indicates balanced option market demand. Trade bias: Neutral EUR/USD, rangebound between SMA20 support and SMA50 resistance. Catalyst: US Nonfarm Payrolls on 6 Nov at 13:30 UTC. Risk: Massive short covering in EUR futures forces a break through resistance at 1.1364.
